questions.q: What is the primary site of gas exchange in the human respiratory system?
a: The trachea
The alveoli
The larynx
The bronchi

questions.q: How are alveoli structurally adapted to maximize the rate of diffusion?
a: They have thick multi-layered walls made of bone
They provide a massive surface area with walls that are only one cell thick
They actively pump gas molecules using muscle energy
They contain rigid cartilage rings to prevent expansion

questions.q: Which gas diffuses from the alveoli into the blood capillaries during external respiration?
a: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Methane

questions.q: Which gas diffuses from the blood capillaries into the alveoli to be eliminated from the body?
a: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen
Helium

questions.q: What keeps the inner surface of the alveoli moist, allowing gases to dissolve before diffusing?
a: A thin layer of moisture/surfactant fluid
Thick mucus produced by the trachea
Liquid blood plasma filling the air space
Pure water secreted by the ribs

questions.q: Why is the diffusion distance between the air in an alveolus and the blood in a capillary extremely short?
a: Because the alveolar wall and capillary wall are each a single layer of flat cells pressed closely together
Because the lungs are compressed by heavy muscle pressure
Because red blood cells touch the outer chest skin directly
Because air pressure forces cells to fuse together

questions.q: What role do the extensive network of capillaries surrounding each alveolus play?
a: They maintain a steep concentration gradient by continuously carrying away oxygenated blood and bringing in deoxygenated blood
They physically pump air back and forth like tiny hearts
They heat up the blood to boiling point
They destroy foreign dust particles using acid

questions.q: What physical factor drives the movement of oxygen and carbon dioxide across the alveolar-capillary membrane?
a: Concentration and partial pressure gradients (diffusion)
Active muscular pumping by white blood cells
Electrical attraction between red blood cells and air
Magnetic pulling forces inside the ribs

questions.q: What happens to oxygen molecules immediately after they diffuse across the alveolar wall into the capillary?
a: They dissolve into the plasma and bind with hemoglobin inside red blood cells
They turn into solid crystals
They combine with carbon dioxide to form water
They destroy the capillary walls

questions.q: Why does deoxygenated blood arriving at the lungs have a lower concentration of oxygen than the air inside the alveoli?
a: Because body cells have continuously used up oxygen for respiration
Because oxygen was destroyed inside the right ventricle
Because the lungs absorb all oxygen during sleep
Because nitrogen gas replaces the oxygen
